name: Techno-populism
summary: Techno-populism combines a populist claim to speak for the whole people against corrupt, obsolete elites and parties with a technocratic claim of competence to deliver results. It prefers action to ideology, disintermediation of parties and unions, and often direct online participation. Scholars see it as spanning left and right and as narrowing democratic choice.
scope: The family described by Bickerton and Invernizzi Accetti (Blair, Macron, Five Star Movement, Podemos) and by Wikipedia's wider usage (digital and online populism, technolibertarian strands), with Five Star's founding Non Statuto as the main primary text. Most economic and social questions are not addressed, so many answers are low-confidence inferences.

sources.usedFor: Five Star's five stars, direct democracy, zero-cost politics, citizens' income, stance on left-right and immigration

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not a defining issue; the strand is post-ideological, but the Five Star Movement and Blair's New Labour both defended public health care, so mild agreement is inferred.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Five Star campaigned on a statutory minimum wage in 2022, but the wider family has no common wage doctrine, so this rests on one case.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Adherents split: the technolibertarian strand favours markets and privatisation, while the Five Star and Chavez cases criticise neoliberalism.

public-ownership.rationale: Mixed: Five Star proposed nationalising the Bank of Italy and opposed water privatisation, but Macron-style technopopulism is market-friendly.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Anti-elite rhetoric targets political and financial elites, but the sources give no common tax line across Blair, Macron and Five Star.

unions-good.rationale: The review says technopopulists weaken intermediary bodies such as unions, mass parties and churches, so they are not champions of organised labour.

property-fundamental.rationale: The sources say nothing on property rights; technolibertarian and populist-left strands would answer in opposite ways.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Anti-monopoly framing (for example blockchain against financial monopolies) pulls one way, privatisation and efficiency pull the other.

cut-welfare.rationale: Five Star's citizens' income proposal shows welfare as a tool against poverty, though Macron-style reformers favour trimming it; net mild disagreement.

worker-ownership.rationale: Technopopulism aims to do existing things better rather than transform ownership, so collective worker ownership is not part of it.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; digital-democracy enthusiasts and security-minded centrists within the family disagree.

legalize-drugs.rationale: No documented common position; the family spans libertarian pirate parties and technocratic centrists.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Not addressed; Pirate-style technolibertarians oppose restrictions while centrist technocrats accept them.

strong-leader.rationale: The authors define populism as including a personal leader's claim to exclusive representation, and technopopulists present themselves as cutting through the messiness of democratic politics to get things done.

state-harmful.rationale: Technopopulists want to govern better, not abolish the state; the review says they aim to do existing things better rather than overthrow them.

limit-guns.rationale: No documented position; the family has no shared line on guns.

empower-police-military.rationale: Not addressed; the issue does not define the strand.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; no shared position across the family.

decide-locally.rationale: Direct digital democracy can be local, but leader-centred technopopulism is national; no shared line.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed by the sources and not a defining issue.

traditional-family.rationale: Inferred from the post-ideological, modernising self-image; Five Star and Macron were not family-values movements, though Lega-allied cases differ.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not a defining issue; the modernising, urban-digital base leans permissive, but Five Star ran a mixed record, hence low confidence.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the modernising, secular style of Macron, Blair and Podemos; no source states it.

more-religion-public.rationale: The review notes technopopulists weaken churches among intermediary bodies and offer a technical, not religious, basis for authority.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed and split between left populists and centrist technocrats.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The reviewer notes nationalism was drawn on by Blair, Macron and Johnson without being central, so adherents are split.

gradual-change.rationale: Technopopulists run against the old politics and claim to cut through institutions, though they do not seek revolution; mild disagreement.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Five Star backed restrictive policies from 2014 to 2019 and the Lega is grouped with the family, while Macron and Podemos are not restrictionist; split.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Five Star is Eurosceptic, Macron is strongly pro-EU; the family is split.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed; the technolibertarian and Macron wings favour it, Five Star and Latin American cases criticise neoliberalism.

nation-first.rationale: Eurosceptic cases lean yes and Macron leans no, so adherents are genuinely split.

open-borders.rationale: Even the family's liberal members (Macron, Podemos) do not call for open borders, and Five Star was restrictionist in 2014-19.

limit-growth.rationale: Five Star has degrowth strands via its environmental roots, but its five stars also stress technological innovation and a green economy; mild disagreement overall.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Environment is one of Five Star's five stars and a large share of its bills, though the family has no common climate doctrine.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The article treats technology as an ideological framework and storyline, and Five Star lists technological innovation among its five stars; optimism is characteristic.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Five Star's ecological roots make it hostile to nuclear power, but the family is not unified and Macron backs it.

revolution-justified.rationale: The review states that technopopulists do not aim at revolution but at doing existing things better.

experts-over-public.rationale: The article separates technocratic populism, which links voters and leaders through expertise, from technological populism, which rejects deference to experts; adherents are genuinely split.

central-planning.rationale: Efficiency and output language and technolibertarian strands do not favour planning, though no source addresses it directly.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed and not a theme of the strand.

basic-income.rationale: Five Star's 2018 program proposed a citizens' income, but this is a single party's measure rather than a family-wide stance.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not addressed; the family has both free-trade and protectionist members.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Not addressed; Macron-style and Five Star-style programs differ.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Technopopulism has no anti-capitalist programme; the reviewed sources show it working within the existing economy.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Five Star proposed nationalising the Bank of Italy rather than abolishing central banking, and blockchain enthusiasts are only one strand.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The review says technopopulists erode intermediary bodies such as unions, which corporatist bargaining would entrench.

one-party-rule.rationale: Five Star explicitly presents itself as a non-party and the family claims to speak for the whole people rather than one ideological party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary rule conflicts with the claim to embody the people's will and with meritocratic and competence appeals.

democracy-best.rationale: The authors see technopopulism as a transformation within democracy, not its end, and technopopulists present themselves as defenders of democracy, though they narrow it.

direct-votes.rationale: Five Star's founding text gives all web users the governing and steering role usually held by a few, and the Wikipedia article calls direct democracy the ultimate technopopulist goal.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils belong to a class-based politics; technopopulism claims the whole people and favours online platforms instead.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not addressed; the claim to represent the whole people suggests no particular sympathy.

natural-rulers.rationale: Technopopulists claim a special competence to rule, which sits with this idea, yet they also claim to embody the ordinary people; split.

political-violence-never.rationale: The authors describe a non-revolutionary, institutional politics, so mild agreement is inferred.

war-builds-character.rationale: Nothing in the sources supports glorifying war; the strand is output- and efficiency-oriented.

separate-church-state.rationale: Inferred from the secular, competence-based claim to rule and from erosion of church influence.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Authority rests on competence and the people's will, not scripture; the review lists churches among intermediaries technopopulists weaken.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Some technolibertarians would agree, but the main figures are state-minded; mild disagreement.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The family claims to represent the people as a whole, not an ethnic group, though nationalist rhetoric appears in some cases.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Technopopulists claim to speak for the whole people and transcend left-right divisions, rejecting class conflict as the main frame.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Not addressed; positions vary from Podemos to Macron.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed, although Latin American cases like Morales are cited.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not a theme; the strand focuses on national politics and technology rather than civilizational blocs.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Not addressed; technolibertarian strands lean yes, populist ones lean no.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Inferred from the technolibertarian and liberal-democratic strands that stress individual participation.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Five Star's integral ecology points yes, but the family has no shared view.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: The strand treats technology as a promise and not a disaster, though Five Star has a green-degrowth wing.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Technology enthusiasm is strong, but the claim to protect the people from disruptive institutions and elites varies; no source states acceleration at the cost of institutions.

algorithmic-government.rationale: The article links technopopulism to ruling by information technology and online platforms, but nothing directly describes AI taking over decisions.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Technolibertarian and blockchain strands support it, centrist technocrats do not; no source addresses it.

restore-past-order.rationale: Technopopulists run against the old politics and present themselves as new, not as restorers of a lost order.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The Persuasion article stresses that technopopulists emphasise action over ideology, and the review says they are not ideologically driven and aim to get things done.

direct-action.rationale: Five Star began with street rallies and online organising but seeks electoral power, so adherents are split.

means-match-ends.rationale: The movement's own online, leaderless form mirrors its stated aims, but the sources do not frame it this way.

return-to-foraging.rationale: The strand treats technology as central, so a return to foraging is the opposite of its outlook.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Competence and expertise claims depend on specialisation, so abolishing division of labour is incompatible.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Left populist cases are critical of capital, but the family as a whole does not hold a Marxist theory of profit.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The strand claims to represent the whole people rather than one class and rejects class dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Not addressed; no support in the sources.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Not addressed; this is a Leninist thesis foreign to the strand.

taxation-theft.rationale: Inferred; even technolibertarian strands in the family work within parties that govern with taxes.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Five Star's founding text puts voice (online participation by all users) at the centre, not exit.

state-as-business.rationale: Efficiency talk and meritocracy suggest sympathy, but customer exit is not documented; split.

media-academia-power.rationale: Anti-establishment rhetoric might agree, but the strand also relies on experts; no source states it.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not a position of the strand and contrary to its modern, inclusive 'whole people' claim.

organic-representation.rationale: Five Star's text rejects mediation by directive or representative bodies, and the review says technopopulists weaken intermediary bodies.

total-state.rationale: Nothing in the sources supports state direction of all life; the strand is post-ideological and works within liberal democratic forms.

national-rebirth.rationale: Technopopulists speak of renewal, but the review ties them to pragmatic delivery, not decadence narratives.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not a theme of any of the cases the sources name.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Authority rests on competence and direct mandate from the people, not feudal oaths.

bound-labor.rationale: Incompatible with a modern, competence-based and democratic claim to rule.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Technocratic populism rests on expertise and technical competence as legitimate bases, which implies knowledge can be neutral, though technological populism distrusts experts.

single-common-good.rationale: The authors say technopopulists claim to represent the people as a whole and deny that politics is a clash of ideologies, which fits a single answer worked out by competence.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Not addressed; direct-democracy ideals might extend to firms but no source says so.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed; privatising and anti-state strands would agree, others not.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Five Star and Podemos are critical of austerity while Macron favours deficit limits; split.

economic-freedom.rationale: The technolibertarian strand agrees but populist-left cases do not.

rule-by-example.rationale: The strand relies on output, institutions and online platforms rather than rulers' moral example.

national-self-determination.rationale: Eurosceptic and sovereigntist cases agree, but it is not a defining claim.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Competence and technical rationality are central to the claim to rule, but emotion and charisma also matter to populists.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Five Star's 2014-19 restrictive stance and Lega allies agree, whereas Podemos and Macron do not; split.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Five Star's citizens' income carried job-search conditions, but no common doctrine; split.

class-collaboration.rationale: The claim to speak for the whole people over a divided society suggests cooperation over class struggle, though no source puts it in these terms.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Not a documented stance; modernising rhetoric does not extend to destroying institutions of culture.

dominated-front.rationale: Hugo Chavez is cited as a technopopulist and held this view, but other members do not; split.

workers-nation.rationale: The strand speaks for the whole people rather than a class, so organising the working class on national lines is not its frame.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Inferred from the modernising, post-ideological outlook; not addressed in the sources.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; blockchain and finance-friendly strands oppose it.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Contrary to the claim to embody the whole people and to every documented case.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The strand denies class framing and sees politics as competence and representation of the whole people.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Five Star's environmental roots and green-economy star point against it, though Latin American cases differ.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Five Star's restrictive turn and Macron's republican assimilationism contrast with Podemos; split.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy theory outside the documented core, though anti-elite rhetoric exists; the cases cited do not espouse it.

proportional-representation.rationale: Five Star pushed for electoral-law input through online votes, but no stable stance is documented across the family.

national-mission.rationale: Not a documented theme in any cited case.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Not addressed; Podemos would agree and others not.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Wikipedia says technopopulism combines anti-elite and anti-political rhetoric, portraying traditional institutions as inefficient, corrupt and obsolete, and Five Star denounced a corrupt political class.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Contrary to the strand's inclusive claim to represent all the people; no documented support.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The technolibertarian strand might agree, but cases like Five Star and Chavez favour active public measures.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: No cited case holds this, and it contradicts the claim to represent the whole people.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Inferred from the claim to represent the whole people; the sources do not discuss it.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Not addressed; not a concern of the strand.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Inferred from secular, modernising orientation; not addressed.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not addressed; no support in any cited case.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Inferred from the secular, competence-based outlook and weakening of church influence.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Technopopulists claim a direct mandate from the people and the review describes their legitimacy as flowing from representing the people as a whole.

population-transfer.rationale: Contrary to the claim to represent the whole people; no cited case advocates it.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: The authors say technopopulists can defend liberal democracy against radical opponents, while Five Star claims to reject party mediation; split.

separated-powers.rationale: The review says technopopulists weaken intermediary institutions and favour disintermediation, and the claim to cut through gridlock sits badly with checks.

vanguard-party.rationale: Five Star's text explicitly rejects party mediation, and technopopulists reject class-based vanguard politics.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Five Star's citizens' income serves the poor but the family has no shared priority; split.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Not addressed; Macron-style reformers lean yes, Five Star and Podemos lean no.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Not a documented theme; inferred from the elite-blame frame.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Five Star's 2014-19 restrictive phase hints agreement, while Podemos and Macron disagree; split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Five Star's citizen-politician ideal and temporary service idea approach this, but lotteries are not a documented proposal.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Not a documented position; the strand claims to defend liberal democracy.

party-controls-media.rationale: The strand uses open internet platforms and online freedom, and no case endorses government control of media.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not a position of any cited case, and the strand rejects party-state fusion.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Five Star's restrictive period leans yes while the other cases do not; split.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Five Star's zero-cost politics principle has elected members cut their own salaries and give up public refunds.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Five Star binds elected members to the online-decided programme, but the strand also rejects party mediation and disciplined cadres; split.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Macron strongly supports it and Five Star in its Eurosceptic phase did not; split.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not addressed; leader-centred cases like Macron fit, Five Star's anti-leader rhetoric does not.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Not a concern of the strand; church influence is among the intermediaries it weakens.

clerical-rule.rationale: Authority rests on competence and popular mandate, not clerical scholarship.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A Leninist position foreign to the strand and no cited case holds it.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from modernising orientation and online openness.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Five Star adopted a two-term limit and later abolished it, while leader-centred cases lean the other way; split.

recall-officials.rationale: Direct online control over elected officials fits Five Star's role for the whole body of users and the disintermediation ideal, though no source names recall by name.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Not addressed; Eurosceptic cases lean yes, Macron no.

people-in-arms.rationale: Not addressed; no support in any cited case.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Five Star's environmentalism has some such sympathies but the strand is digital and urban; split.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Anti-elite rhetoric agrees, but technocratic populism leans on university-trained expertise; split.

death-penalty.rationale: Inferred from the modernising orientation of the main cases; not addressed.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Inferred from the secular, modernising orientation; not addressed.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The competence and technology emphasis is incompatible with creationism in schools.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Not addressed; libertarian strands disagree, others lean yes.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not a documented position; Macron and Podemos disagree, and Five Star did not campaign on it.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Latin American left cases might agree, but it is not a documented position of the strand.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Podemos and Latin American cases like Chavez used constituent processes and the strand favours participatory rewriting; inferred.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The review frames technopopulists as defenders of liberal democracy, though output orientation leaves some openness; mild disagreement.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine with no connection to the strand and no cited case holds it.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Meritocratic and technolibertarian strands agree; the whole-people claim and left cases do not; no source addresses it.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed; populist-left cases would agree and market-friendly ones would not.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Not addressed; Macron's France holds one, other cases have no view.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: A personal leader's direct claim to represent the people fits direct election, though the sources do not discuss the mechanism.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Five Star proposed nationalising the Bank of Italy and populists distrust unelected bodies, though Macron accepts independence.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Not addressed; no shared view across the family.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Five Star's ecological roots and opposition to incinerators suggest support, but the family has no common line.

collective-defense.rationale: Not addressed; Macron supports alliances, Eurosceptic cases are more sceptical.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: The review says technopopulists erode church influence as an intermediary body, but no source says they curb church property.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Not addressed; leader-centred cases claim to stand above parties, which fits, but no source states it for heads of state.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Authority rests on competence and a popular mandate, so sacred or divine descent is alien to it.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed; technolibertarian strands might agree, left populists would not.

space-expansion.rationale: Technology enthusiasm gives some sympathy, but no source states it.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: The strand attacks corruption and presents itself as law-abiding; Five Star bars candidates with criminal records, but strong-leader features cut the other way.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The claim to speak for the people as a whole and to bypass intermediaries sits against balancing rule among few and many.

leader-cult.rationale: Five Star's founding text claims to give governing roles to all users rather than one leader, though personal leadership is documented.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Maoist position foreign to the strand.

land-redistribution.rationale: Latin American cases might agree; not documented for the strand overall.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Not a documented position of any cited case.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Contrary to the secular, competence-based outlook.

women-must-cover.rationale: Contrary to the secular, modernising outlook of the cited cases.

common-currency.rationale: Macron supports the euro, while Five Star in its Eurosceptic phase questioned it; split.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Not a documented theme; the strand focuses on national politics.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Not addressed; the technology-as-storyline framing hints at it, but no source states a theory of history.

ban-cartels.rationale: Anti-elite and anti-monopoly rhetoric (such as blockchain against financial monopolies) suggests mild agreement.

no-bailouts.rationale: Anti-elite populists often oppose bank bailouts, whereas technocratic centrists accept them; split.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The review says technopopulists weaken intermediary institutions, and populism favours majority will, though Macron-style liberal technocrats would differ.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: An autarkic bloc is foreign to the strand and no cited case holds it.

moral-incentives.rationale: Output, efficiency and meritocracy are the strand's stated values, not moral incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The review states technopopulists do not aim at revolution, still less armed revolution.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Meritocracy and anti-elite rhetoric suggest agreement, though the sources do not discuss titles.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: No cited case holds this and it contradicts the strand's democratic claims.

patriotic-education.rationale: The reviewer notes nationalism appeared in Blair, Macron and Johnson, but it is not a defining theme; split.

public-money-creation.rationale: Five Star's talk of nationalising the Bank of Italy points that way and blockchain currency strands point elsewhere; split.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Not addressed; Macron's France has such ties but the sources do not treat them as part of the strand.

delink-world-market.rationale: Latin American left cases criticised neoliberalism but the strand is not delinking; mild disagreement.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: A Leninist thesis foreign to the strand.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: The technolibertarian strand might agree, but the claim to represent the whole people points the other way.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Liberal technocrats favour entrenchment, populist majoritarians do not; split.

elective-rulers.rationale: The strand claims a popular mandate and rejects hereditary rule, though it does not address the question as framed.

minority-veto.rationale: Technopopulists claim to act for the whole people and push past gridlock, so a single-member veto is alien.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Authority is placed in a leader's mandate or direct online votes more than in parliament; split.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed; Five Star's environmental roots lean toward concern, mild agreement inferred.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The strand opposes elite privilege and speaks for the people against elites, so it frames duty differently.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The movement's founding text calls on all users to take part in governing.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Latin American left cases agree, but it is not a documented position of the strand.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Not a documented theme of any cited case.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not addressed; Morales is cited but no source addresses it.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Five Star calls itself post-ideological and refuses ideological labels; split.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the strand's lack of revisionist themes.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The strand works through electoral and online politics and presents itself as defending democracy, though Latin American cases differ.

office-by-exam.rationale: Competence and meritocracy are stated values, suggesting mild agreement, though Five Star's citizen-politician ideal pulls the other way.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Eurosceptic and Latin American cases agree, Macron's market-friendly cases do not; split.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Inferred from the secular, modernising outlook; not addressed.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The founding text places governing power in all users and bypasses representative bodies, suggesting bound and removable representatives, though recall is not named.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Not addressed; privatising strands lean yes, Five Star leans no.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Not addressed; inferred as foreign to the strand.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The authors portray the strand as working within democratic institutions, so mild agreement is inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Five Star's green-economy and degrowth strands agree, but the technology-optimist strand does not; split.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Not addressed; not a documented theme of any cited case.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Not addressed; a Soviet-era doctrine foreign to the strand.

corporate-influence.rationale: Anti-elite rhetoric targets political and financial elites, so mild agreement is inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: Five Star's citizens' income pairs with job-search conditions, but no common line across the family exists.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: The strand claims to defend liberal democracy and pursue delivery within existing institutions.

industrial-unions.rationale: The strand weakens unions as intermediaries and has no organising preference.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The strand claims to represent the whole people and no cited case holds this view.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Not addressed; inferred as a position none of the cited cases advance.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Five Star's online platform and transparency commitments aim at making political proceedings visible to members.

local-production.rationale: Five Star's green economy leans yes, other cases do not.

informal-organisation.rationale: Five Star began as an informal online platform and non-association, but it contested elections and later formalised, so adherents are split.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Eurosceptic cases agree, Macron does not; split.

religious-nation.rationale: The strand claims the people as a whole and weakens churches, not a religion-defined nation.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Not addressed; the anti-elite outlook is opposed to ritual submission.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Not addressed; Lega-linked cases might agree, others not.

defeat-communism.rationale: The strand is post-ideological and anti-communism is not a stated theme.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Not addressed; Blair and Macron lean yes, Five Star leans less so.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Not addressed; technolibertarian strands agree, Five Star and Latin American cases do not.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not a documented theme and at odds with the technology-oriented outlook.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Not addressed; the strand works through national politics, not communal withdrawal.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The strand claims to transcend left-right, which resonates with a third course, but it offers no systemic alternative.

holocaust-denial.rationale: No cited case holds this, and it contradicts the strand's liberal democratic claims.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Contrary to the modernising outlook of every cited case.

suppress-opposition.rationale: The review sees technopopulists as defenders of liberal democracy against radical opponents, not as suppressors of opposition.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Contrary to the secular, competence-based outlook.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Foreign to the strand and no cited case holds it.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Contrary to the secular outlook and the claim of popular mandate.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The Non Statuto sets out that all users take part in consultation, deliberation and decisions, and Wikipedia treats direct democracy as the ultimate technopopulist goal.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Not addressed; Podemos would agree, others would not.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: The Persuasion article says technopopulism spans and transcends left and right, and Five Star was conceived as post-ideological and rejects the divide.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Five Star's restrictive phase on immigration did not become a cultural-incompatibility claim in the sources; mild disagreement inferred.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Authority is placed in the people and in competence, not in God.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Macron's France enforces it, other cases are silent; split.

social-market-economy.rationale: Not addressed; Blair and Macron lean yes, others have no stated view.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Five Star's later support for a common European army suggests it keeps armed forces.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Five Star's wavering foreign alignment and Macron's Atlanticism give no common line.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary leadership contradicts the strand's claims of competence and popular mandate.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Five Star and Podemos criticised austerity while Macron's type does not; split.

property-franchise.rationale: The strand claims to represent the people as a whole and favours broad participation.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Anti-elite rhetoric might agree, but the strand relies on online media and the sources do not address it.

racial-franchise.rationale: Contrary to the claim to represent the whole people.

online-participation.rationale: The Non Statuto gives the internet a central role in joining, consultation, deliberation, decision and election, and Five Star later ran the Rousseau platform.

open-government-data.rationale: Five Star's online platform let members trace and vote on legislative proposals, but publication of records is not stated.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Contrary to the secular outlook of the cited cases.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: The strand claims to represent the whole people and no cited case holds this.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Randomly drawn deliberation is a participatory device the strand's direct-democracy outlook favours, but it is not documented.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Anti-elite and anti-monopoly rhetoric suggests mild agreement.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the modernising outlook; not addressed.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The strand is secular but not anti-religious, and no cited case promotes atheism.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: The claim to speak for the whole people against intermediaries favours direct majority mandates over communal power sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Five Star's citizens' income shows a state role in poverty relief.

term-limits.rationale: Five Star treated politics as temporary service and barred anyone elected twice from running again, until the limit was abolished in 2024.

vote-delegation.rationale: Online platforms like Rousseau enable such delegation but the sources do not state it as a position.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Inferred from the modernising outlook; not addressed.

missingStatements.text: Political parties and other intermediary bodies should be bypassed in favour of direct links between leaders or platforms and citizens.
missingStatements.rationale: The Non Statuto rejects mediation by directive or representative bodies, and the reviewed scholarship describes technopopulists as weakening parties, unions and other intermediaries.

notes: Contested: whether technopopulism is an ideology at all, since the scholars treat it as a style spanning left and right. Strands differ: technocratic populism trusts experts, technological populism does not.
